properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 15 at 11:36AM MST until September 17 at 5:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...All of northern Arizona, including Apache, Navajo,
Coconino, Yavapai and northern Gila counties.

* WHEN...From late tonight through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Flash flooding will be possible in creeks, normally dry
washes, swimming holes, and over recently burned areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Increasing moisture will combine with a shortwave feature moving
north across Arizona to bring multiple rounds of showers and
thunderstorms from late Tuesday night through Wednesday night.
Thunderstorms will have the potential to produce heavy rainfall
that could lead to flash flooding, especially in areas that
receive repeated rounds of rainfall.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Have a way to receive Flash Flood Warnings and be prepared to take
action should warnings be issued.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Southeast Arizona, including the following
areas, Baboquivari Mountains, Catalina and Rincon Mountains,
Chiricahua Mountains, Dragoon and Mule and Huachuca and Santa Rita

Graham and Greenlee Counties.

* WHEN...From this evening through Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be
flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Well above normal moisture levels for September are expected to
result in scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms capable
of producing heavy rainfall from late tonight through late
tomorrow night. Rain totals of 1 to 2 inches are expected with
the stronger storms with isolated amounts over 2 inches possible.
Areas that received substantial rainfall over the previous few
days will be more susceptible to flash flooding. This rainfall
will result in faster response in washes, creeks, and storm
drainages.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Recent heavy rainfall combined with potential for repeated rounds
of thunderstorms this evening and overnight will lead to a flash
flooding threat through at least Tuesday morning. Additional
rounds of rainfall will be possible through the remainder of the
week. If confidence increases in potential for heavy rain Tuesday
night into Wednesday, part or all of the watch may need to be
extended.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH FRIDAY AFTERNOON

properties.areaDesc: Two Rivers; Fairbanks Metro Area
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 14 at 3:36PM AKDT until September 19 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Including the following areas, Fairbanks, North Pole, Two
Rivers, Fort Wainwright, Ester, and Fox

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rain may result in minor flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The Chena River is running higher than normal and will continue
to be high through the week. More rain is expected beginning
Tuesday and will continue through Wednesday afternoon. Storm
total rainfall during this time will be around 0.50" to 1.00". It
has been very wet lately and this amount of rain has the
potential to bring the Chena and Little Chena Rivers above minor
flood stage beginning Wednesday.

- This means low-lying and typical flood-prone areas may
experience areas of flooding from Wednesday through the end of
the week as water levels gradually rise then fall. In addition,
while we are not expecting much flooding away from rivers,
streams and creeks, as the ground is already saturated and may
struggle to hold more water. This can lead to pooling and ponding
of water across the area which may make travel difficult in
localized spots.

- There is some uncertainty with exact timing and amounts of
rainfall but as details become clearer, we will continue to
update.

- For more updated river information, please refer to
water.noaa.gov or weather.gov/aprfc

- Http://www.weather.gov/aprfc
